trigger: member_set_owned's ResultSetError->ScopeEvalError::Kind split (NotFound/NotOwner->OwnerCheckFailed, DbError->StoreDegraded) is a manual boolean check rather than an exhaustive switch, so a hypothetical future ResultSetError variant would silently fall into the StoreDegraded else-branch

trigger: live_presence() holds presence_cache_mu_ across the live Postgres query whenever the 3s cache is stale
summary: Reporter's own facts (global lock-step latency under concurrent load during a presence-store outage) are real, but git -L history (commit de4f24172, an earlier unrelated merged PR) proves the lock-held-across-I/O pattern predates #4981 PR-1 unchanged in shape, frequency, or duration.
adjudicated_by: claude-orchestrator, cross-verified by chaos-injector's independent recommendation to file this as its own follow-up issue
adjudication_rationale: De-escalated from the reporter's BLOCKING label because the derived band on the ACTUAL facts (I5 base MEDIUM, E0 no raise) is SHOULD, and because git history (git log -L on agent_registry.cpp) proves this PR introduces zero delta to the mechanism. Real, valid finding on its own merits; not this PR's regression. Filed to issue #5026 rather than fixed here.

trigger: dispatch_due durably stamps last_dispatched_at for every claimed policy before kickoff_check runs, so a degraded kickoff_check strands the policy until default_interval_seconds elapses
summary: This exact scenario was already raised, adjudicated, and mitigated (warn log + yuzu_server_policy_eval_errors_total counter) in an earlier governance round, cited by name in the code's own dated comment (#3495, governance Gate 4 unhappy-path, 2026-08-30, UP-1/UP-2). This PR only routes two new ScopeEvalError Kinds through that same, already-instrumented path -- it does not weaken the existing mitigation.
adjudication_rationale: Rediscovery of an already-adjudicated, already-mitigated design tradeoff (see the code's own #3495 comment block, policy_evaluator.cpp:505-548). Not a new defect introduced or widened by this PR's actual diff.

trigger: a crash or audit-store hiccup between the two independent, non-transactional audit.resolution_failed / audit.evaluation_aborted calls on the ladder's abort path
summary: Real new code (added beyond the original design brief), but the underlying dispatch decision is already safely aborted regardless of the audit-write outcome -- an evidentiary-completeness gap under a rare crash-timing window (I7/MEDIUM), not a security-control failure (I1/I2). Independently converged: unhappy-path and compliance-officer both raised this without having seen the other's report.
adjudication_rationale: Reporter's own BLOCKING label does not survive a facts-first re-derivation: no I1/I2 applies since the security decision is unaffected by whether the audit write itself succeeds. Real gap, filed rather than fixed given the broader chokepoint redesign it implies.

trigger: yuzu_scope_eval_degraded_total/yuzu_scope_resolution_failed_total increment unconditionally even when the paired audit write fails

adjudication_rationale: Same rationale as up3-audit-pair -- forensic-completeness gap, not a security-control failure.

trigger: member_set_owned's query never filters ttl_at, despite a doc comment claiming OwnerCheckFailed covers 'absent, expired, or not owned'

adjudication_rationale: Speculative with no current trigger or exposure -- no code path today exhibits the concern.

trigger: when a from_result_set: owner-check failure and a presence-store outage are both live in one evaluate_scope call, only OwnerCheckFailed surfaces -- the result-set preload short-circuits before live_presence() is ever probed
summary: Audit-completeness gap only -- the dispatch itself still correctly fails closed either way, regardless of which reason surfaces.

trigger: PolicyEvaluator's 10s tick always exceeds the 3s presence-cache TTL, so every dispatch_due tick during a sustained outage still pays a full blocking query
summary: Query cadence during a sustained outage is byte-identical before and after this PR -- the negative cache was never intended to help a caller whose own interval already exceeds the cache TTL, and did not regress that caller's behavior in either direction.
adjudication_rationale: No behavioral delta introduced by this PR at this call site; restating the reporter's own observation as a NEW defect of this diff does not hold up against a before/after comparison.

trigger: evaluate_scope_local's arm-nothing-on-abort means a transient CustomPropertiesStore/TagStore hiccup during a Guardian toggle-push cycle means the new enable/scope toggle does not reach the affected agents for that push attempt
summary: Reporter's own report states this is 'unchanged by this PR' -- identical to the pre-split evaluate_scope semantics for these three call sites. Re-read against server.cpp:18876-18928: these are single-rule TOGGLE pushes (H1 scoping), not a full periodic re-sync -- a hiccup means the new toggle fails to reach affected agents this attempt (I6, a deliverable not reached), not an active revocation of an already-armed rule's existing enforcement (which would be I1). No evidence of false assurance to the operator was found in this snippet; the raw sent-count path was not traced further. Out of scope for a diff that only splits (does not change) this behavior.
adjudication_rationale: Reporter's own text concedes this is unchanged by the diff under review. IMPACT corrected from an initial I1 misreading to I6 after re-reading the actual push-protocol semantics (toggle delivery failure, not active disarm of standing enforcement); SHOULD is the facts-derived band, not a de-escalation from a higher one. Filed as a design-discussion item rather than fixed in this PR, which introduces no delta here.

trigger: to_abort_reason's no-match fallthrough defaults to the specific-but-wrong DbDegraded rather than an explicit unknown
summary: Unreachable in practice: -Werror=switch is wired in server/core/meson.build, so an unhandled enumerator is a compile error, not a runtime fallthrough.
adjudication_rationale: Compile-time protected today (E6: wrong outcome proven unable to occur in production).

trigger: has_any_reachable()'s fail-open-on-degrade plus the negative cache means a genuinely unreachable fleet during a real outage can take up to one query-acquire-timeout window to reach the correct classification rather than a cheap short-circuit

trigger: crossing kQueryRowCap=100000 live agents flips fleet-wide evaluate_scope from success to a hard PresenceDegraded abort, purely from ordinary fleet growth/connect-disconnect flicker at the boundary

Pre-PR1 behavior silently truncated past the cap with NO signal at all; this PR turns that into an explicit, correctly-classified abort -- a safety improvement, not a new defect, mischaracterized as a regression by the reporter.
adjudication_rationale: git-log-confirmed pre-existing cap; the change direction is strictly safer (loud abort over silent wrong-answer). Closed the residual operator-disclosure gap by documenting the boundary behavior in metrics.md rather than filing separately.
